## About

Source: https://www.charliecheesman.net/about/

About

AI deployment strategist based in London.

Before that: 5 years at EY-Parthenon advising Fortune 500 and FTSE 100 companies. Set up the
EY-Parthenon AI Lab and wrote the UK AI strategy. Clients spanned F1, Formula E, US retail, and
PE-backed tech.

In August 2025: built, launched, and sold a company in 20 hours at a Stockholm hackathon - the
fastest exit in Europe. That became the20hr.co.

Also founder of Unicorn Mafia, a
developer community of 1000+ engineers across the EU and US.

Oxford Economics & Management following dropping out of Durham Engineering.

On the web

- Business Insider Consulting - the race to become AI-native

- ETN 60x - the future of AI business models

- Dagens Industri the20hr.co - a company built and sold at Lovable's 20-hour hackathon

- The Times Unicorn Mafia - the power of communities to create companies

- BNN Unicorn Mafia - a 16-year-old's journey from Latvia to London to SF

- EdTech Innovation Hub Unicorn Mafia - embodied AI hackathon sponsored by Anthropic

## Ideas

Source: https://www.charliecheesman.net/ideas/

Ideas

A collection of ideas at various stages of development.

- Net Zero from Day Zero There will come a day when all new companies will be Net Zero
from the day they start. There should be a platform that enables this.

- The Dual Rationality Hypothesis The
Joint Hypothesis Problem can
be generalised to any test for rationality. Any test for rationality requires a model of
rationality to test against, meaning models of rationality can never fully be rejected.

- Ideaware Ideas can be thought of as software for thinking. In the same way as you
have a Tech
Stack, you can have a Personal Idea Stack. Your idea stack is the collection of ideas you use
to interpret the world.

- Impact Arbitrage Why doesn't charitable giving behave like investing? Because there
is no impact arbitrage. There is (1) no absolute metric for impact and (2) no means to trade
impact among givers. If there were, charity would look more like
effective altruism. We could
change this.

- An AMC for Carbon Taxes Why don't companies voluntarily commit to an AMC for carbon
taxes? This would incentivise governments to introduce a carbon tax.

- A Marketplace for AMCs Advance Market Commitments
will soon be privatised and apply to many markets. There should (and soon will) be a marketplace
for AMCs.

- Comparative Advantage for Startups Comparative Advantage explains
why startups can outcompete incumbents. They have a lower opportunity cost to effort.

- Confidence Expectations A variable for confidence is the missing link between
Rational Expectations and
Behavioural Economics.

- Learning Efficiency in AI Systems Learning efficiency as a measure of AI
intelligence. How many repetitions of a game does it take for the AI system to become good,
relative to a human?

If some of these are interesting to you, reach out.

## Questions

Source: https://www.charliecheesman.net/questions/

Questions

Thoughts and questions I keep coming back to.

- Intertemporal Fairness In what sense is it 'fair' to be born in one time period vs
another?

- Intelligence as being General Purpose Intelligence is how general purpose something
is.

- The Cost of Signalling Stereotyping is the cost of our reliance on
signalling.

- Branding Diseconomies Brands suffer from
diseconomies of scale.

- The Market for Nimbyism Why don't we have a market for
Nimbyism?

- Meal Deals Why are there no
meal deals in other countries?

- Memory Palaces Why are we not all taught how to build
memory palaces?

If some of these are interesting to you, reach out.
